# Results

**Current numbers: [SCOREBOARD.md](SCOREBOARD.md).** It is generated by `python -m bench.scoreboard`
from `tables/*.json`, which describe the code now on `main`: round 19 plus the round-20 Mandarin
word step and the Korean / Japanese speed-up. They come from the round-19 frozen run of the
held-out benchmarks (2026-11-22), with every Mandarin row re-run on `main`'s code the same day;
for the other nine languages `main` gives bitwise-identical outputs, so their rows stand (Azure
from cached responses only). Plus the round-20 Spanish false-alarm fixes (number readings, glides):
their Spanish rows come from one held-out run of 2026-11-23, and every other language is bitwise
identical to the code above ([round20_fa_release_check.md](round20_fa_release_check.md), which also
has the English, German, French and Korean fixes that the rule kept off). The benchmark scripts score
with the fp32 Scorer. What round 19 changed, with before / after rows and everything that
got worse: [round19_integration.md](round19_integration.md); the Mandarin re-run, the tally and
everything worse than 1.0.2: [round20_release_check.md](round20_release_check.md).

The scoreboard and the README describe version 1.1.0, released on 2026-11-24. The numbers for 1.0.2 are
the scoreboard at tag `v1.0.2` (frozen run of 2026-11-17, after the license-clean refit:
[licence_refit.md](licence_refit.md)).

**Other assessment systems on real learner speech: [learner_benchmark.md](learner_benchmark.md)**
(OpenPronounce, Azure, Lingolix and a Chivox sample, in four languages, with size, memory and time).

Regenerated by that run (their numbers are current):

| file | script |
|---|---|
| `english_vs_azure.md`, `tables/english_vs_azure.json` | `bench/eval_english.py` |
| `languages.md`, `tables/languages.json`, `tables/swap_ours_vs_azure.json` | `bench/eval_languages.py` |
| `cv_real.md`, `tables/cv_real.json` | `bench/eval_cv.py` |
| `ompal.md`, `tables/ompal.json`, `tables/ompal_tone_zh_v3z.json` | `bench/eval_ompal.py` |
| `tables/coaching_azure_yardstick.json`, `tables/coaching_12b_heldout.json`, `tables/coaching_r4_heldout.json` | `bench/coach/azure_yardstick.py`, `heldout_12b.py`, `fit_r4.py eval` |
| `tables/contrast_audit_test.json` | `bench/audit/contrast_audit.py --split test` |
| `tables/length_runtime_ja.json` | `bench/length/heldout_runtime.py` (the shipped length channel) |

`tables/round15_length_heldout_ja.json` is the round-15 offline measurement (its script,
`bench/length/heldout.py`, was removed because it no longer matched the runtime after round 17).

Everything else here is a **historical write-up of one design round** (`round*.md`,
`calibration.md`, `coaching.md`, `prosody.md`, `tone_v3.md`, `phase2_evidence.md`,
`contrast_audit.md` = the validation-split audit, `azure_swap.md` = Azure's own swap tables). Their
numbers describe the system at that round and were measured before later rounds; where they differ
from the scoreboard, the scoreboard is current. `tables/round1` … `tables/round4` hold the
earliest held-out tables, kept for the before / after comparisons in those write-ups.
